docs.title: Project Structure
docs.snippet: This is the PyTorch Tutorials website (pytorch.org/tutorials), built with Sphinx and Sphinx Gallery.

docs.title: Build
docs.snippet: - make html-noplot — builds HTML without executing tutorial code. Fast, no GPU needed. Use this for quick validation of RST/Sphinx structure. - make docs — full build that downloads data, executes all .py tutorials, and produces the final site. Requires a GPU-powered machine…

docs.title: Linting
docs.snippet: - lintrunner -m main — lint changes relative to the main branch - lintrunner --all-files — lint all files in the repo

docs.title: Testing
docs.snippet: - make html-noplot is the quick sanity check for RST and Sphinx errors. - Full execution of .py tutorials runs in CI on GPU shards. - To test a single tutorial: GALLERY_PATTERN="my_tutorial.py" make html

docs.title: Tutorial File Format
docs.snippet: - Interactive tutorials are .py files using Sphinx Gallery conventions. Filenames should end in _tutorial.py. - Non-interactive tutorials are .rst files. - Data dependencies must be added via .jenkins/download_data.py, not the Makefile. Follow the existing patterns in that file.…

docs.title: Adding a New Tutorial
docs.snippet: 1. Place the file in the appropriate *_source/ directory based on difficulty level. 2. Add a customcarditem entry in index.rst (or recipes_index.rst for recipes). 3. Add the tutorial to the corresponding toctree in index.rst. 4. Add a square, high-resolution thumbnail image to…

docs.title: Coding Style Guidelines
docs.snippet: - Minimize comments; be concise; code should be self-explanatory. - Match existing code style and architectural patterns. - Tutorial prose should be written for a global audience with clear, easy to understand language. Avoid idioms. - Use active voice in tutorial instructions.…

docs.title: Contributing to tutorials
docs.snippet: We want to make contributing to this project as easy and transparent as possible. This file covers information on flagging issues, contributing updates to existing tutorials--and also submitting new tutorials.

docs.title: Issues
docs.snippet: We use GitHub Issues to track public bugs. Please ensure your description is clear and has sufficient instructions to be able to reproduce the issue.

docs.title: Security Bugs
docs.snippet: Facebook has a bounty program for the safe disclosure of security bugs. For these types of issues, please go through the process outlined on that page and do not file a public issue.

docs.title: Contributor License Agreement ("CLA")
docs.snippet: In order to accept a pull request, you need to submit a CLA. You only need to do this once and you will be able to work on all of Facebook's open source projects, not just PyTorch.

docs.title: License
docs.snippet: By contributing to the tutorials, you agree that your contributions will be licensed as described in the LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.

docs.title: Updates to existing tutorials
docs.snippet: 1. If you haven't already, complete the Contributor License Agreement  ("CLA"). 1. Fork the repo and create a branch from  main. 1. Test your code. 1. Lint your code with a tool such as  Pylint. 1. Submit your PR for review.

docs.title: New Tutorials

docs.title: Managing data that is used by your tutorial
docs.heading_path: Managing data that is used by your tutorial
docs.snippet: Your tutorial might depend on external data, such as pre-trained models, training data, or test data. We recommend storing this data in a commonly-used storage service, such as Amazon S3, and instructing your users to download the data at the beginning of your tutorial.

docs.title: Python packages used by your tutorial
docs.heading_path: Python packages used by your tutorial
docs.snippet: If your tutorial has dependencies that are not already defined in requirements.txt, you should add them to that file. We recommend that you use only mature, well-supported packages in your tutorial. Packages that are obscure or not well-maintained may break as a result of, for…

docs.title: Submission Process #
docs.snippet: Submit your tutorial as either a Python (.py) file or a reStructuredText (.rst) file. For Python files, the filename for your tutorial should end in "_tutorial.py"; for example, "cool_pytorch_feature_tutorial.py".

docs.title: Add Your Tutorial Code ##
docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Add Your Tutorial Code ##
docs.snippet: 1. Put the tutorial in one of the  beginner_source,  intermediate_source,  advanced_source  based on the technical level of the content. For recipes, put the  recipe in  recipes_source.  In addition, for recipes, add the recipe in the recipes  README.txt  file.

docs.title: Include Your Tutorial in `index.rst`#
docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Include Your Tutorial in `index.rst`#
docs.snippet: In order for your tutorial to appear on the website, and through tag search, you need to include it in index.rst, or for recipes, in recipes_index.rst.

docs.title: Link ###
docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Include Your Tutorial in `index.rst`# > Link ###
docs.snippet: The link should be the path to your tutorial in the source tree. For example, if the tutorial is in beginner_source, the link will be beginner_source/rest/of/the/path.html

docs.title: Tags ###
docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Include Your Tutorial in `index.rst`# > Tags ###
docs.snippet: Choose tags from the existing tags in the file. Reach out to a project maintainer to create a new tag. The list of tags should not have any white space between the words. Multi-word tags, such as “Getting Started”, should be hyphenated: Getting-Started. Otherwise, the tutorial…

docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Include Your Tutorial in `index.rst`# > Image ###

docs.title: Submit the PR ##
docs.snippet: NOTE: Please do not use ghstack. We do not support ghstack in the pytorch/tutorials repo.

docs.title: Do not merge the PR yourself ##
docs.heading_path: Submission Process # > Do not merge the PR yourself ##
docs.snippet: Please **DO NOT MERGE** your own PR; the tutorial won't be published. In order to avoid potential build breaks with the tutorials site, only certain maintainers can authorize publishing.

docs.title: Asking a question
docs.snippet: If you have a question about a tutorial, post in https://dev-discuss.pytorch.org/ rather than creating an issue in this repo. Your question will be answered much faster on the dev-discuss forum.

docs.title: Submitting an issue
docs.snippet: * Feature request - request a new tutorial to be added. Please explain why this tutorial is needed and how it demonstrates PyTorch value. * Bug report - report a failure or outdated information in an existing tutorial. When submitting a bug report, please run: python3 -m…

docs.title: Contributing
docs.snippet: We use sphinx-gallery's notebook styled examples to create the tutorials. Syntax is very simple. In essence, you write a slightly well formatted Python file and it shows up as an HTML page. In addition, a Jupyter notebook is autogenerated and available to run in Google Colab.

docs.snippet: When you submit a new tutorial, we encourage you to keep it in sync with the latest PyTorch updates and features. Additionally, we may contact you to review any PRs, issues, and other related matters to ensure the tutorial remains a valuable resource.
